packs/core/JOURNEY.md:300 is a live 404 on the published site because sync_pack_journeys copies journey bodies verbatim and a Markdown body link is not base-qualified the way docsUrl is; it is the only guide link across 20 JOURNEY.md files, so packs have no working way to link a guide page, and the rendered-site link audit did not cover the journeys route

388 broken relative Markdown links across 92 files with no gate resolving them; the adopter-facing seed subset is separately gated and deferred, so the open work is deciding the domain for the internal corpus, where a gate over frozen specs would red on records nobody may edit

The shipped intent, spec, plan and brief templates carry their author guidance as HTML comments, so every artifact made from them contains raw HTML a CommonMark editor drops or shows verbatim. Measured 2026-09-24 with markdown-it-py over the repository: 543 of 921 spec and plan files, 53 of 104 RFCs, 26 of 154 intents and 5 of 20 briefs are affected, 891 tokens in total, of which 201 are multi-line blocks. intent-template.md alone ships 20. Fixing the templates is what stops new artifacts inheriting it; a sweep over existing files is separate and is NOT purely mechanical, because nine intent comments carry content rather than guidance (five discovery-chain rungs, one deliberate product-vision altitude, and three recording that a needs edge is stated but unenforced), the Status annotations are the only place a reader sees the lifecycle enum, and scanner-suppression-and-pin-hygiene.md contains the literal <!-- --> in prose as one of four comment syntaxes, so a regex sweep corrupts that sentence

The third defect, infra-decisions.md's false seven-to-eight correspondence claim, was fixed by b59becf26 on 2026-09-24

RFC-0098 D4/D6 mandate uninstall --skill <name> for a direct row, routed to the pack-keyed file-ownership removal path and mutually exclusive with --pack. The CLI has no --skill and requires --pack, so that form does not exist; removal works only via uninstall --pack <identity> --yes. No removed criterion carried this. It also owns the removal completeness direct-skill-lifecycle F8 measures: a file a later revision drops stays on disk unowned, and ownership-keyed removal alone cannot reach it.

Re-read what an installed direct skill declares: allowed-tools, metadata.boundaries, metadata.credentialed, the SKILL.md digest, and every payload digest, per skill. Probed 2026-09-01: show, list-installed --format json, and the state file each carry none of them, so an adopter who consented at install has no route back to what they agreed to. The show contract sets additionalProperties false over a closed key set docs/specs/okf-catalogue-discovery owns, so that spec needs amending alongside.

Receipts for direct commands report kind, name, source, resolved revision, digest, scope, adapter, and the matching update and uninstall commands. Delivered for install and shipped, but its criterion (AC22) left the direct-skill-repository-installation final list, so the guarantee is unowned; the upgrade route this narrowing builds adds a second receipt surface.

Install, validate, and list-installed grammar clauses that left with AC7 and AC9: list-installed adds no new flag and --no-check, --offline, and --check-drift keep their meanings; a catalogue row whose drift was never computed renders an em dash rather than a 0; and the exit-2 set for bare upgrade, bare primitive upgrade, bare uninstall, bare install, conflicting pack/profile, pack/profile with a direct source, and upgrade --pack P --scope local. AC7/AC9 at c794be99c are the authority.

Manifestless list-installed rows: KIND column, INSTALLED/LATEST as an em dash, numeric DRIFT, the JSON schema-version increment, --updates-only exclusion, and the sentinel reaching no surface. Also AC22's shipped guarantees: no outbound request, STATUS always unknown, no ahead state, no source-digest comparison in footprint drift. AC22 at c794be99c is the authority; it and AC26 stayed on direct-skill-repository-installation's final list, the narrowed follow-on owning identity and upgrade only.

Local scope across the direct lifecycle: projection, .agentbundle-local-state.toml, the git exclude, the tracked-path refusal, and rollback. RFC-0098 D6 admits it for standalone skill upgrade while the shipped route refuses --scope local; the parent spec withdrew its AC24 local-scope clause as unsatisfiable.

Hand-authored canonical-equivalent and expected-normalized fixtures for every direct shape and sub-form, including the collection category level whose flattening to skills/<leaf>/ is the behaviour parity exists to pin, AC24's rule that no canonical, direct, or expected-normalized fixture is generated with code under test, and the assertion the fixtures feed: repo and user projections and per-file plans are byte-identical through both renderers. AC24 at c794be99c is the authority.

The author-facing documentation RFC-0098 D8 names: the skill-repository format reference with its stable raw schema URL, the make-a-skill-repository-installable how-to, install-routes and reference page updates, docs-site navigation, the --help surfaces install, validate, upgrade, uninstall, and list-installed, and a local-path-only coding-agent prompt. Left the final list with AC23.

Capability re-consent on upgrade: the difference rendering including old/new digest, revision, added and removed skill names, the full payload delta, and executable-mode omission for old data; the refusal axes, --accept-new-capabilities bound to the recomputed digest, unknown drift refusing even with the flag, and upgrade --all applying it to every row before any write. Left the final list with AC30 and AC9.
Discharge the behavioural half of the provider-absence obligation: evaluate a pre-registered fixture-and-expected-result mode, judged by an independent reviewer, against an executable absence harness

Two of nine adjudicated findings on the withdrawn cooling-scope-closure amendment remain open; the file records each closure with its evidence. Open: a plan whose Done-when requires editing a hash-frozen plan.md, which nothing detects at approval time; and AC31 being unable to fail when the release surfaces agree at a version whose published code differs from what ships. Both need an owner decision rather than a repair

Two of three RFC-0096 receipt follow-ons stay open. Entry-removal precondition: reassigned to rfc0096-wave7c-pruning -- stranding harm refuted by measurement, but nothing makes the file and entry removals atomic and a record field cannot supply that. Cooled cross-repo deferral slug: still Wave 7b's. Reclassified schema gap: closed by docs/specs/reclassified-lifecycle-result/. Both settled in rfc0096-wave7c-lifecycle-record-decisions.md; the linked notes file is frozen, so status lives here

A state-lock reclaim's identity check and its rename are two operations, so a holder acquiring between them is displaced and reports StateLockLost having done nothing wrong. Not closable by checking harder -- POSIX has no rename-if-unchanged. Atomic takeover is disproved and recorded: rename replaces unconditionally, so every contender with the same stale snapshot wins in turn, measured at three to five holders. The note carries the forced-interleaving reproduction

Two RFC-0096 Wave 7c follow-ons. (1) rfc0096-wave7c-pruning: a pruning session must prove its own precondition -- an artifact's file and its workspace entry must be removed together -- and nothing makes the two removals atomic. (2) Moving AC23-pinned files falsifies cooling-scope-closure's AC23 TITLE and its Durable Outputs line "neither may change"; the AC body still holds, so the repair is a retitle. Caused by this delivery and Wave 7b; its owner restates it. RFC-0096:380 names the slice

Two open RFC-0096 Wave 7b follow-ons. A declared-empty source.parent on a cooled entry is trusted not verified, needing a closeout-time writer in close-work. An interrupted run of the shared-test dedup guard strands collectable test files in the repository root, which gitignore hides but does not prevent. Two are closed: the pack-script citation conflict, and the two AC17 test names that contradicted their bodies, renamed in the live tests on 2026-09-30
